catalog.summary: Stacked sections that expand and collapse.

rootRole.reason: The pattern names no role for the set. A group of headings is already an outline the reader can navigate; `group` on top of it would announce a container the APG never asks for, and `region` would put every accordion in the landmark list.

wiring.aria-disabled: true on the trigger of the one open item while requireOpen holds the set from emptying
wiring.headingLevel: handed to every item, which renders the heading element itself
wiring.aria-label: the consumer's own, and only when the set is a named region the page needs

keyboard.effect: toggles the panel of the focused header; with `multiple` off, the panel that was open closes with the reason `select`
moves to the next focusable element; every focusable element in the accordion is in the page tab sequence
moves to the previous focusable element, under the same rule
moves to the next header and wraps at the end when loop is on; opens nothing
moves to the previous header and wraps at the start when loop is on; opens nothing
moves to the first header that is not disabled
moves to the last header that is not disabled

keyboardDeparture.reason: The arrows were optional guidance in the accordion pattern and were removed; Base UI has since deprecated both `loopFocus` and `orientation` on its accordion, stating that the orientation state no longer affects keyboard focus behavior. Radix and Ark still ship them and readers have learned them, so they are shipped here additively: nothing writes tabindex, every header stays in the page tab sequence, and the keys move focus and change nothing else.
keyboardDeparture.cost: A key that does something the pattern does not name. A reader who expects ArrowDown to scroll the page inside the header row does not get that; every other element in the accordion, including everything in an open panel, still does.

orientation.reason: Radix and Ark both ship a horizontal accordion and Base UI has deprecated its own. A horizontally stacked set of sections of which one is open is a tab list, and `tabs` shipped in this wave with the marker, the scrolling list and the pattern's own keyboard model.

onFocusChange.reason: Ark alone reports which header has focus, and `onFocusIn` on the root is the same information from the platform: `onFocusIn={(event) => read(event.target.dataset.value)}`.

roleGroup.reason: No surveyed implementation and no line of the pattern puts a role on the set. A container announced around an outline the reader can already navigate is one more thing to move past.

variantMapping.reason: The group hands each item a variant through the binding and selects nothing inside it. A rule reaching [data-ui='collapsible'] from this stylesheet would make one family's DOM part of another's contract, which is the rule `checkbox-group` set.

requireOpen.appliesTo: the trigger of the one open item
requireOpen.reason: "If the accordion panel associated with an accordion header is visible, and if the accordion does not permit the panel to be collapsed, the header button element has aria-disabled set to true." The APG's own example is the only surveyed source that ships it.

imperative.openAll: opens every item that is not disabled, with the reason `programmatic`
imperative.closeAll: closes every item, with the reason `programmatic`, unless requireOpen holds the last one
imperative.reason: Angular Material ships both on `mat-accordion`. A controlled consumer already owns the array and needs neither; an uncontrolled one has no array to set, which is the case an escape hatch exists for.
